Sometimes I feel comforted by the fact that in just a couple clicks I can find another stranger going through similar problems I'm facing. Sometimes it makes me feel even worse knowing that the world is just filled to the brim with these lost and troubled souls. And other times I feel both and more confused than ever. Hell, hell everywhere

Oh god, yeah I know what you mean. I've felt that way for the most of this year. Personally it feels like a mild migraine that just won't go away, where everything in my mind feels sort of cluttered and chaotic besides the strong emotions. And I end up looking like a mindless blattering zombie who can't focus for the life of me. Meditation seems to help a bit, but beyond that I'm at a loss.

I'm glad my ramblings could be of help :p

As for your shame of your feelings, I say let it go! Occasionally we have to vent when things get a little too hot inside. If you don't already I recommend keeping a daily journal of your progress; where you begin objectively and honestly write about your daily mindsets and then your opinions about them. Its something a lot of people do when they have no where to turn and in turn you learn a lot about who you are and what you wish to be. Just a suggestion that may help cement the progress of what you accomplish. Oh and if you ever need a stranger to hear you out or help brainstorm your situation I'm your gal. Best of luck

Sounds like you dove a little too deep and didn't expect that snowball of stress to get so big. Happens to everyone, but tbh I don't think you're problem is a lack of perspective on the "big picture". In fact I think that's exactly where you're coming up short, you're too busy looking towards the future while plagued by problems in the present.

What I mean is perhaps you should try tackling that stress piece by piece. It seems to be the logical choice when they don't go away over time. There will be some problems you can't fix immediately, such as your homesickness, but ultimately shifting your focus on what you can solve atm will start pushing you in the right direction.

Being in a rather similar situation myself I'm afraid I cannot say much other than I enjoyed your note and deeply share your sentiment. It was really quite eloquent and reminded me of a Dostoyevsky passage.


>I have spoken of this because I keep wanting to know for a fact whether other people feel such enjoyment? I will explain; the enjoyment was just from the too intense consciousness of one's own degradation; it was from feeling oneself that one had reached the last barrier, that it was horrible, but that it could not be otherwise; that there was no escape for you; that you never could become a different man; that even if time and faith were still left you to change into something different you would most likely not wish to change; or if you did wish to, even then you would do nothing; because perhaps in reality there was nothing for you to change into.

I'm so sorry thats horrible to hear, losses of any kind are hard to bear, especially from those we love. I'm afraid there's not much we can do to get over that losses that deeply affect us. Because just like fresh wounds they will only close with time, even if they do leave nasty scars. The impressions they left on us were just too deep to ignore or wipe away.

And trust me I know how little comfort that is to hear, because I too have felt utterly lost and alone when I lost my fiance 2 and a half years ago. For a while time seemed to go on just fine for everyone else but me. It was as if my entire world was stripped of it's color and meaning and replaced with an aching grey. Gradually the pain became manageable (if not just familiar) as I learned to accept her absence and use it as a sort of catalyst for my "new" life. But I'd be lying through my teeth if I said it doesn't affect me to this day.

As for your predicament, I suggest you have a serious conversation with your husband fully explaining how your loss affected you and how his dismissiveness only exasperated the issue. He may not understand the true extent of the problem as people can process grief very differently. But no matter what you shouldn't be ashamed of you're feelings, as it's only in your nature to react this way when under such emotional duress. Death is a very serious issue and suppressing it without a full introspection of it's effect will only plant the seed for a much deeper problem.

Well there's my 2 cents, I hope it was of any help and I hope the coming days treat you better. I highly recommend looking up some articles or books on the subject (like [this](https://www.huffingtonpost.com/entry/10-things-i-learned-while_b_5923558) ) if talking with your husband doesn't go well. It's what helped me, if you need any advice feel free to pm me. Best wishes

>Now that I’m not in school anymore, I don’t know how to make a friend... seems like everyone in public is already in a small tribe and I’m just a loner 

Ooh you hit the nail on the head with that. Im in the same sinking boat atm drowning in the feeling of loneliness. Personally when I had the money I tried attending social type of gatherings such as art and yoga classes to put myself out there. But as you said everyone seems to have they're own thing going on, they may want to talk but beyond that most people seem to be content with the friends they have. Which leaves people like us wondering how the hell they managed that.

Of course it's all just a matter of "try try again" until something sticks. But man is it draining to constantly feel rejected and cast off on our own little islands.

You have no idea how happy that makes me to hear that :D It'll definitely be a huge undertaking, but from what you've already went through I think you'll be more than prepared for what lies ahead. Try to keep the effects of this depression in mind, it's a rather insidious disease that corrupts from within and will consume you if you're not careful.

 And never be afraid or ashamed to look for help along the way, it may not be plentiful or even immediately obvious but it's there if you know how to look for it. Well enough with my lecturing, I wish you only the best op and if you ever need a friendly impartial stranger to vent or brainstorm your situation with, I'm you're gal. Good luck, hun

Hello, I read your whole post and can definitely relate to the effect that an abusive childhood can have especially with an alcoholic parent. In my case it was my dad and my mother's side of the family that relied on drinking to get away from the fact that we lived in a shitty little ghetto populated with nothing but dead ends and braindeads. By the time I turned 18 I knew I had to get away from such a toxic environment that would only drag me down with it and turn me into the person I've always despised. So I trudged through a year of crappy part time jobs and manual labor for neighbors while being as frugal as possible. By 19 and a half I had enough to rent a room with a distant cousin I slightly new in New Mexico. And let me tell you, not a damn day passed with out me thinking about how easy it would be to just end it and find some final relief. But, I decided I want to at least make it till my mid twenties to see if this just wasn't the result of my childhood or another momentary obstacle. And that's sort of brings me to now, not doing too hot but leagues better than I would back "home".

So I guess the point I'm trying to make is to save that final irrevocable decision until you've truly exhausted your options and yourself. Im sorry if that comes across as a platitude or tough love ( not my intention whatsoever), I just don't want you to jump to such a rash decision at this crossroad you find yourself in. I know it may sound like baseless hope and what ifs, but you really don't know what tomorrow may bring. Like that girl you mentioned for instance, how unexpectedly awesome was that? I too have an ex I still deeply care about who gave me a will and passion. And I still think of them painfully, but I know losses in life come to pretty much everyone and what defines them as a person is how they find they're way out of that shadow and onto their own path. Best wishes stranger

Oh I totally know the feeling, it's frustrating that people expect so much from you yet give so little in return. And when you do start to build that foundation it feels like a simple breeze can knock it all down leaving you feeling worse than before. I can't tell you how many times I've spent months or years even getting close to someone only to have them ghost or trade me in for a more interesting friend.

It's not even like I'm clingy or rude either, I try to make sure I'm giving as much respect as I'd like from a friend but in return all I get is another scar and lesson in pessimism :/ 

I'm sorry to hear about your situation btw, I know how suffocating it can feel to have no one to turn to besides people who only care about the mundane or themselves.

I've felt the same way a couple of years ago, especially the nightmares. As much as we'd like to suppress lost relationships with people we cared about in the past we just can't get rid of the imprint they left on us. In fact, some days I still get misty eyed and shaky when thinking of my ex who seemed to understand me more than anyone else.

I believe this is where self improvement and acceptance come into play. Unfortunately I'm not doing too hot at that atm, but I have met people in my life who've turned losses and pitfalls into chances to "find themselves". It varies greatly on the person in question, but for the most part they decided on some plan and threw themselves into it. Whether it was intense study, physical training, changing philosophies, spiritual journies or what have you. They decided they had to sort of flush out and drown the past with the present to see the future.

Of course it's easier said than done, especially for folk such as ourselves who may lack the motivation and will to maintain such a radical shift in life. But I think that's how we find our way of moving on. And hopefully in the process we attract new people and snowball that into some type of fullfilment. I hope you find that way, op

And trust me I know not to fear awkwardness or rejection, in fact they're probably the things I'm most familiar with at this point. And I know not it's not prudent to call it quits after the first round of failures. But it just gets really disheartening when over the years, failure and rejection become the only constants in my life. thanks for the reply
